summary: Selene Horizon is an advanced lunar south pole solar illumination, horizon obstruction, and direct-to-Earth communication mission planner. It utilizes open-source NASA cutting-edge information and technology to properly overlay data in a visualization easy to understand and plan for missions. The app is formatted such that beginners-experts in aerodynamics can understand by toggling between levels of comprehension.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

Selene Horizon is an interactive planning and analysis tool for lunar south pole missions. It helps mission planners, researchers, educators, and students evaluate potential Artemis landing sites by calculating exact Sun and Earth visibility against the Moon's rugged crater terrain.

How it works:

  • Terrain Ray-Marching: Using high-resolution elevation maps from NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (at 5 m/pixel and 30 m/pixel), the app traces sightlines outward from any landing coordinate. It calculates the surrounding horizon angle while adjusting for the Moon's curvature (1,737.4 km radius) and the height of a lander's solar panels and antennas.
  • Sun & Earth Tracking: The app calculates precise Sun and Earth positions relative to the lunar surface (benchmarked against NASA JPL Horizons data) to find their exact sky angles over any chosen timeframe.
  • Power & Communication Estimates: It evaluates grazing sunlight across the Sun's 0.53° angular width to predict solar power output (in W/m²), tracks Direct-to-Earth radio windows by accounting for lunar wobble (libration), and calculates signal travel time.
  • Interactive Maps & Radar: It combines a 360° horizon skyline view, a sky-dome radar, and an interactive NASA Moon Trek map featuring official Artemis III candidate zones and real-time shadow simulations.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Replaces Complicated Tools: Traditional spaceflight tools require complex command-line scripts or clunky query forms. Selene Horizon turns that data into a clean, visual interface that gives instant answers.
  • Fixes Terrain Accuracy Issues: Standard global Moon maps often accidentally measure deep crater floors instead of narrow ridge peaks. Selene Horizon uses high-resolution data and crest-snapping so high-altitude sites like Connecting Ridge and Malapert Massif show accurate, unobstructed horizons.
  • Side-by-Side Site Comparison: Planners can compare multiple landing zones at once on an interactive scatter plot (comparing Sunlight % vs. Earth Communication %) to quickly find the best launch windows and battery requirements.
  • Easy Data Export: Users can verify results directly against live NASA JPL Horizons queries, paste in custom horizon profiles, and export full CSV spreadsheets for outside power and trajectory modeling.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • For Mission Planners & Engineers: Speeds up early mission design, rover path planning, and backup communication scheduling for Artemis and commercial lunar landers.
  • For Educators & Students: Makes orbital mechanics easy to grasp by visually showing why the Moon's slight 1.54° tilt creates grazing sunlight and why Earth appears to bob up and down near the horizon.
  • For the Public: Opens up complex NASA planetary archives so anyone can explore where astronauts will soon land on the Moon.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Core Web Stack: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
    • NASA JPL Horizons System (DE441) for live position verification.
    • NASA LRO LOLA elevation models (SPole875_5mp_v04 at 5 m/px and SPole75_30mp_v04 at 30 m/px).
    • NASA Moon Trek for surface maps, Artemis III boundary polygons, and illumination data.
    • IAU 2015 / NAIF SPICE standards for lunar coordinate transformations.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Adaptive Complexity Modes: Selene Horizon has four user levels (Introductory, Intermediate, Advanced, and Expert). Switching modes doesn't just rewrite text—it reshapes the layout, charts, and data density:
    • Introductory uses simple compass directions, plain-English status tags, and basic geometry.
    • Expert unlocks multi-decimal telemetry, exact line-of-sight margins, trajectory residuals, and full engineering breakdowns.
  • Field-Notebook Design: Instead of looking like a cluttered spreadsheet, it blends an aerospace dashboard with a clean, tactile field-notebook aesthetic featuring subtle paper textures and smooth animations.
  • Synced 3D Perspectives: It links a 360° horizon view, a polar sky radar, and a surface shadow map together in real time, making complex 3D space geometry immediately obvious.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Lunar Curvature: Adjusting sightlines for the Moon's 1,737.4 km radius, since distant crater rims drop noticeably below a flat geometric plane.
  • True Sun Size: Modeling the Sun as a 0.53° wide disc rather than a single pinpoint, allowing realistic simulations of partial shadows and gradual solar power drop-offs along crater rims.
  • Lunar Wobble (Libration): Accounting for the Moon's 5.14° orbital tilt and elliptical orbit, which causes Earth to drift in an apparent monthly box (±6.7° vertically, ±7.9° horizontally) near the horizon.
  • Data Transparency: Linking every chart, elevation pixel, and coordinate directly back to official, citeable NASA repositories and API endpoints.
  • Accessibility & Offline Resilience: Building a responsive design with touch controls, mobile navigation, keyboard-friendly tours, and built-in fallback math so the app still works when internet bandwidth is low.

Source Code: https://github.com/robot3-track/nasa-selenehorizon-mhc1
